subject: Re: Request for temporary burst + GPU tier variance — Rosen DataWorks
messages:
From: Eli Rosen <eli@rosendata.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@rosendata.com>, Rachel Ortiz <rachel.legal@rosendata.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary burst + GPU tier variance for Q2 peak

Kim and Lauren —

Quick context: Rosen DataWorks (platform analytics) is entering a 6-week performance window starting next Monday. We’ve identified a short-term spike in inference throughput tied to a regulatory ingestion requirement. Our dedicated pool (reserved) is healthy, but we anticipate sustained 25–35% above reserved tokens/hour during 06:00–14:00 PT for the next 6 weeks.

Can Redwood:
- Allow temporary burst capacity of up to 35% over our reserved baseline for six weeks (2027-04-19 through 2027-05-30) with a reservation hold so we don’t lose priority capacity?
- Temporarily map a subset of our workload to H100-class SKUs during critical windows (we can tolerate cold-starts outside those windows) — customer asks this for latency SLAs.
- Apply a capped overage rate or a 20% discount on standard overage pricing for that period, or offer a one-time credit to offset the cost impact.

I attached our utilization export and a short calc. We need a decision by EOD Tuesday to finalize engineering changes.

Eli
Eli Rosen
CTO, Rosen DataWorks
eli@rosendata.com

We’ll aim to get a formal answer by EOD Tuesday.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: temporary burst + GPU tier variance for Q2 peak — cost impact

Kim / Lauren / Vivek —

I ran a short workup from finance and pricing. Key points: 
- If we allow a 35% burst on current reserved baseline for 6 weeks mapped to H100-class for the critical window only, incremental cost exposure (at list overage) is ~$185k.
- Options we can offer without setting a precedent that hurts SKU discipline: 
  1) Temporary burst cap at 25% (not 35%) for six weeks + H100 mapping for 06:00–14:00 PT windows; customer pays overage at list.
  2) Burst cap at 25% + H100 mapping + one-time credit equal to 40% of expected incremental overage (~$74k credit) to smooth commercial impact.
  3) Allow 35% but charge list and add a 30% reservation-hold fee (keeps capacity priority) — higher revenue, less customer goodwill.

My recommendation: option 2. Provides a measurable concession without rewriting our template for reserved SKUs. Requires an exec approval for the one-time credit and the reservation-hold exception. See attached cost_impact_workup.xlsx.

If Lauren signs off, we can draft the short amendment and route to legal and finance for a DocuSign. We’ll include telemetry triggers (if sustained >50% for 5 consecutive days we reevaluate).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Pricing & Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
attachments: cost_impact_workup.xlsx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T14:11:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: temporary burst + GPU tier variance for Q2 peak — approval

Kim / Karthik —

Approved with conditions. Summary of executive decision: 
- Approve option 2 as proposed by Karthik: allow temporary burst at 25% for six weeks, enable H100 mapping for the 06:00–14:00 PT windows, and provide a one-time credit equal to 40% of estimated incremental overage (~$74k).
- Reservation-hold: approve a conditional hold for the six-week window, but require a hard cap at 35% — we will not backfill their capacity in the hold window beyond the approved tolerance.
- Require telemetry/lifecycle guardrails: if Rosen exceeds 50% over baseline for 5 consecutive days, the amendment triggers immediate review and we can pause burst. 
- Legal to prepare a short amendment and finance to approve the credit issuance. We should include a limited-liability clause and a single-use exception flag on their account (so this does not become a template).

Kim — you have my signoff to convey approved terms to Rosen and push the amendment through DocuSign. Please include Rachel Ortiz (Rosen legal) on the outbound so we capture their acceptance.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Phone: +1 650 555 2201

Date: 2027-04-13T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary burst + GPU tier variance for Q2 peak — APPROVED (next steps)

Eli / Maya / Rachel —

Good news — executive approval granted. Summary and next steps: 

Approved terms (concise):
- Temporary burst allowance: 25% above reserved baseline for six weeks (2027-04-19 to 2027-05-30).
- H100 mapping: allowed for critical window only (06:00–14:00 PT).
- Commercial concession: one-time credit equal to 40% of estimated incremental overage (~$74k).
- Reservation hold: conditional hold enabled for the six-week window; hard cap will not exceed 35% and we will not reassign held capacity during that period.
- Telemetry guardrail: if usage >50% for 5 consecutive days, we will pause burst pending joint review.

What I need from Rosen to finalize:
1) Confirm baseline reserved SKU and committed hours in writing (reply to this thread).
2) Legal to review & sign the short amendment — I’ve attached the proposed amendment and shared a DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-ROSEN.
3) Confirm acceptance by EOD Wednesday, 2027-04-14, so we can coordinate engineering changes and capacity reservations.

I’ve looped in Karthik and Lauren (commercial) and Vivek for visibility. Finance will issue the credit once the DocuSign is executed. We’ll also put the one-time exception flag on the account so this does not automatically generalize to future deals.

Thanks — we’ll move fast once you confirm.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
